source.title: Symphony No. 9, Op. 95 — III. Scherzo. Molto vivace

bars.description: Printed bars 1–59 twice, then 60–175; trio 176–190 with first ending 191, then 176–190 with second ending 191; 192–238 twice, then 239–247; D.C. 1–141 without repeats, then coda 248–299. The source numbers both trio endings 191 and inserts an unperformed full-bar spacer after 247: six-quarter source extents preserve those encoded coordinates, while performed fragments select three quarters each. There is no pickup. The source MIDI is canonical, not a complete unfolded performance.

endpoints.basis: Initial source-pitch energy inspection windows, not listening annotations: opening E octaves and the final short E-minor tutti after the written general pause. These broad initial windows require fresh overlay inspection before publication.

provenance: Mutopia1793 provides the full orchestral movement, not a reduction. Its third movement has no trombone/tuba staff; triangle is present and is retained as a source-defined unpitched percussion part. MIDI percussion key 81 is a triangle identifier, not a claim of sounding A5.
All fourteen sounding MIDI tracks are assigned to thirteen named source parts; the two genuine horn staves are grouped. Instrument identities come from Mvt3_Scherzo.ly, never General MIDI patches.

Clarinets in A already sound down three semitones through the source transposition a; horns and trumpets use source transposition e and documented changes to c and back. The bass_8 source already places double basses at sounding pitch: initial MIDI E3 (52), one octave below cello E4 (64), with E1 (28) later. No additional transposition is applied.

The source conductor has 299 printed bars, 3/4 throughout, explicit repeats at 1–59, 176–191 and 192–238, D.C. al coda after 247 and a coda jump after 141. The MIDI includes both bar-191 endings and a silent spacer before the coda but does not execute these repeats or D.C. Recording recurrence and harmonic correspondence remain subject to fresh diagnostics.

The published MIDI advances violin I/II by 0.1015625 quarter after its second-ending grace; other parts retain integer-quarter final attacks. This source-specific clock discrepancy is disclosed and must be inspected against a common-clock modern compilation before publication.
All alignment is provisional and not checked by ear. Source note durations represent warped notation, not measured bow releases or percussion decay.
